title: Go CLI Runtime and product iteration proposal
test_convention: Every TestName listed in verification is planned and does not imply an existing test. Acceptance must assert each exact name occurs in go test -list output before running it, and must also run the complete affected package race suite; a -run command with zero matches is never sufficient.

waves.title: Stop immediate user harm and make evidence trustworthy
waves.gate: R0 hotfixes have red-before-fix behavior tests and pass after fix; raw verification failures remain archived and new gate result is tied to the tested commit.

waves.title: Run ownership and recoverable transcript MVP
waves.gate: One authoritative Run outcome, truthful cleanup state, complete committed session restore, and no automatic replay of unknown side effects.

waves.title: Provider, permissions, UI and service-entry closure
waves.gate: Provider, capability, approval, session, terminal and event contracts are consistent across shipped entry paths; each lane can parallelize after shared contracts are reviewed.

waves.title: Extension boundaries, UI quality and release evidence
waves.gate: Every claimed extension/UI/telemetry capability has a default-path or protocol conformance proof, or is clearly marked unavailable.

waves.title: Optional verified cross-process action resumption
waves.gate: Deferred until a product decision; no general shell/MCP replay without verifier, receipt, fencing and reconciliation.

phases.title: Stop immediate harm and establish trustworthy gates
phases.parallelism: Independent hotfix slices and validation-gate work may run in parallel; do not delay immediate fixes for a broad Runtime refactor.

phases.title: Run terminal outcome, cancellation and resource ownership
dependencies: R0 hotfix contracts; R0 gate work may continue
phases.parallelism: Stream terminal, Run quiescence and bounded cleanup builders can work after the shared state/ownership contract is reviewed.

phases.title: Durable session identity, journal and recovery MVP
phases.parallelism: Session identity and JSONL recovery work can be separated after the durable-record schema and single-writer contract are fixed.

phases.title: Provider resolution, stream reliability and context policy
dependencies: R0 credential-routing hotfix; R1 terminal contract; R2 transcript schema for compaction integration
phases.parallelism: Provider factory and context/production policy slices are separable after interface contract review.

phases.title: Tool effect capabilities, approvals and bounded execution
dependencies: R0 approval/data-integrity hotfix; R1 execution-state contract
phases.parallelism: Approval policy and filesystem/schema/output slices may proceed independently after common ToolEffect semantics are reviewed.

phases.title: TUI interaction and transcript journeys
dependencies: R0 ask_user hotfix; R1 terminal/event contract; R2 session identity
phases.parallelism: History rendering and input/editor workflows may proceed after a single-session projection contract is agreed.

phases.title: CLI, ACP, MCP and Web entry contracts
dependencies: R0 network/credential hotfix; R1 terminal contract; R2 session identity; R4 capability/approval scope
phases.parallelism: CLI/trust and ACP/MCP adapter slices can proceed in parallel after session/capability identity is fixed.

phases.title: Extension, skill, tracing and audit lifecycle
dependencies: R1 lifecycle contract; R4 capability model; R6 support-version contract
phases.parallelism: Extension lifecycle and tracing/privacy work are separable.

phases.title: UI rendering quality and product capability disclosures
dependencies: R5 TUI workflow; R6 entry support matrix; R7 telemetry/privacy decisions
phases.parallelism: Terminal quality and dormant-feature disclosure can be delivered as independent slices.

phases.title: Opt-in verified cross-process action resumption
dependencies: R2 recovery MVP; R4 capabilities; R6 transport identity; explicit product decision
phases.parallelism: No implementation until the product decision and action verifier/receipt contract are accepted.

tasks.title: Define immediate hotfix contracts and gate truth
tasks.user_story: As a CLI user and maintainer, I need known destructive, credential, approval and deadlock failures to have explicit safe outcomes and trustworthy regression evidence.
tasks.goal: Turn immediate high-impact findings into narrow, independently testable fixes and pin the current verification baseline without waiting for a Runtime redesign.
deliverable: Red-before-fix acceptance cases for one-time approval, malformed write/edit args, wildcard without auth, provider credential routing, ask_user delivery, Streaming Bash output cap, MCP origin/retry behavior, and trace prompt redaction.
A local/CI verification matrix recording the raw make verify failure, NO_COLOR-cleared race pass, scan 20 ERROR and CI filtering mismatch.
verification: Review each case against its source finding and mark default, explicit-config or dormant reachability.
Do not treat archived bug-reproducer PASS output as a passing fix: translate it into an expected-correctness test, show it fails on the audited baseline, then passes after the change.
Protected Makefile/CI/rules/task metadata are not edited under this proposal; route any required protected change through the repository approval chain.
tasks.commit_spec: Designer creates a reviewed contract note and named red-before-fix cases; no product-code commit is required.

tasks.title: Fix one-shot approval and malformed file mutations
tasks.user_story: As a user, an Allow-once decision must authorize one execution only, and a malformed write/edit request must never silently clear existing data.
tasks.goal: Fix ApprovalAllow caching and reject missing/wrong-typed write.content and edit.new_string at both schema and execution boundaries while preserving explicit empty strings.
deliverable: Updated approval cache semantics with explicit AlwaysAllow scope.
Required tool schemas and defensive executor/queue validation.
Regression tests proving rejected calls leave the original file byte-for-byte unchanged.
verification: Planned tests: TestApprovalAllowOnlyAuthorizesCurrentCall, TestWriteMissingContentPreservesExistingFile, TestEditMissingNewStringPreservesMatchedText, TestExplicitEmptyContentClearsFile.
Assert exact test names through go test -list, run affected packages with -race -count=1, and exercise the CLI middleware path.
tasks.commit_spec: One focused commit for approval and malformed mutation behavior after red-before-fix tests exist; keep unrelated safety changes out.

tasks.title: Close immediate network, credential and prompt privacy failures
tasks.user_story: As an operator, an explicitly unauthenticated listener must not expose wildcard interfaces, credentials must not cross provider/origin boundaries, failed MCP calls must not be replayed blindly, and traces must not persist raw prompts by default.
tasks.goal: Fail closed on the concrete dangerous combinations and remove credential forwarding or duplicate side-effect paths before broad provider/service work.
deliverable: Wildcard plus no-auth is rejected or bound to explicit loopback with a clear error.
Provider selection validates protocol, credential scope and origin before sending any request.

MCP endpoint origin is pinned before any configured Header/Bearer/OAuth credential is sent; this is a prerequisite to exposing those credentials in CLI config because current CLI config does not expose them. Ambiguous post-dispatch failure is returned as unknown without retry.
Prompt-bearing trace/log attributes are redacted or disabled by default through every actual tracer.
verification: Planned tests: TestServeNoAuthWildcardRejected, TestProviderCredentialNeverSentToWrongOrigin, TestMCPRejectsCrossOriginEndpointWithCredentials, TestMCPCallUnknownDoesNotReplay, TestDefaultTraceContainsNoPrompt.
Use loopback httptest servers and verify the second origin receives neither request nor credential; exercise the actual CLI factory and tracing wiring.
tasks.commit_spec: One commit per isolated service/provider/privacy boundary fix, with each risky path red before the patch and green afterward.

tasks.title: Unblock ask_user and bounded-output subprocesses
tasks.user_story: As a TUI user, an ask_user request must reach an input handler; as a user of streaming shell, output truncation must not block a finite child process forever.
tasks.goal: Add the missing UI message update route and keep draining child pipes after capture limits while bounding retained output.
deliverable: HITL request/response is correlated and cancellation wakes the waiting request.
Concurrent approval requests retain separate IDs/results and cannot overwrite one pending slot.
Streaming Bash drains/discards excess output after the retained cap and reports truncation without turning a finite command into timeout.
verification: Planned tests: TestTUIAskUserMessageReachesHandler, TestAskUserCancelUnblocksWait, TestTUIConcurrentApprovalRequestsRemainResolvable, TestStreamingBashDrainsPastMaxOutput.
Subprocess output must exceed OS pipe capacity; assert return before deadline, bounded stored output and no lingering reader goroutine.
tasks.commit_spec: Keep the UI message fix and pipe-drain fix in separate commits so each regression can be bisected.

tasks.title: Make source-level verification coverage and failure reporting trustworthy
tasks.user_story: As a maintainer, the local and CI gate must run the intended packages and fail honestly on scanner errors, missing tools, bad JSON or zero behavior tests.
tasks.goal: Make direct source-level test and scanner gates explicit, hermeticize color-dependent tests, inventory build tags/skips, and make scanner/RunVerify failures actionable without changing protected default Makefile/CI wiring.
deliverable: Source-level direct test commands cover cmd/cli and named mock/e2e tagged suites; the execution copy does not claim the protected default Makefile/CI target includes them.
Tagged suites and skip inventory have named entrypoints and reasons.
Scanner and verification output distinguishes static hint, skipped evidence and behavior-tested pass; no source path may blanket-ignore a rule or swallow execution/parse failure.
Formatting checks are read-only and tool versions are recorded; protected default gate wiring is split to R0-PROTECTED-GATE-01.
verification: Planned tests: TestVerifyDoesNotPassOnZeroBehaviorTests, TestScannerProcessFailureFailsGate, TestScannerInvalidJSONFailsGate, TestGateIgnoresExternalNoColorForANSIContractOnly.
Run exact source-level test and scanner commands on a clean commit in the original host environment and with NO_COLOR cleared; preserve full logs, reports and exit codes.

Check exact expected test names before targeted execution; run full affected package race suites. A scanner or source-gate error remains visible and cannot be reclassified as a protected-gate approval.
tasks.commit_spec: Source-level implementation only. Protected Makefile, workflow, linter and infra rule edits belong to R0-PROTECTED-GATE-01 and require their explicit approval process.
tasks.execution_scope: Source/test-canary cleanup maps 2d4b79→a8717d0. Five named race tests passed in 1.080s and the scanner gate passed; root also reran make scan at a8717d0 with 354 files, 0 ERROR and 1,448 WARN. This does not establish a complete make verify pass or protected release review, so R0-BLD-04 remains in progress.

tasks.user_story: As a maintainer, I need the reviewed source-level gates connected to the repository defaults after the protected patch is explicitly approved.

deliverable: A separately reviewable proposed patch for the specific protected Makefile, CI workflow or repository rule changes needed to connect the already-tested source gates.
After explicit approval of the exact patch, integrated default commands invoke the intended tests/scanner and fail closed on missing tools, malformed output, zero behavior tests, or scanner errors.
No scanner exemption, ignored finding, severity downgrade or swallowed error is used to make the default gate pass.
verification: Before applying any protected change, present the exact diff and record explicit user approval; absent approval, keep this task pending and do not modify protected files.
After approval and integration, run the exact default Makefile/CI-equivalent gate from a clean commit and preserve command, environment, snapshot hash, full output and exit code.
Independently verify every source-level scanner finding is either fixed or separately justified as a genuine false positive; never suppress it to green the gate.

The earlier make scan failed at b7ffe0b, but the source/test-canary repair maps 2d4b79→a8717d0 and the fresh make scan at a8717d0 passes with 0 ERROR and 1,448 WARN. tasks.goal: Review each R0 source fix against the original failure, valid red/green evidence, and correct local source-level test/scanner results; this acceptance gate is sufficient for downstream engineering but does not accept protected default wiring.
deliverable: Review report maps every R0 source case to source location, compiled red baseline, green fix, integrated commit and affected-package race evidence.
Commit-bound local test and scanner logs state exact command, environment, snapshot, test registration, findings and exit status.
Remaining scanner warnings, source errors, false positives and tagged skips are listed without suppression; source-level acceptance is explicitly distinct from protected release-gate acceptance.
verification: Run full affected package race suites and actual CLI child-process/fixture tests at the reviewed source snapshot.
Run the correct direct source scanner and source verification commands from a clean worktree at that snapshot; assert exit codes, exact registered tests and no false-green command substitution.
Independently verify each proposed false-positive explanation against the rule and triggering source; scanner findings cannot be hidden to pass.

tasks.title: Independently review protected default-gate release wiring
tasks.user_story: As a release owner, I need proof that each immediate fix closes its source-confirmed failure without hiding the original evidence.
tasks.goal: Review only the explicitly approved protected-gate patch and prove the repository default/CI entrypoints run the accepted source gates without suppressions.
deliverable: Independent review report ties the approved protected diff to exact default and CI-equivalent commands and records any remaining release blockers.
Commit-bound gate output demonstrates the tested default entrypoints fail on prohibited scanner errors and cannot false-green.
verification: Confirm a recorded explicit user approval exists for the exact protected patch before accepting any protected-file change.
From a clean integrated commit, run default Makefile and CI-equivalent gates and inspect full logs, actual test registration and scanner findings.
Reject scanner allowlists, ignored findings, severity downgrades or swallowed command errors used to obtain a green result.
tasks.commit_spec: This is the protected release-review child mapped to source task R0-REV-01. Overall source task R0-REV-01 remains incomplete until both mapped review children are accepted.

tasks.title: Add a plan-mode fail-closed stopgap
tasks.user_story: As a user requesting read-only planning, I need currently known and unknown mutating tools blocked while the complete capability model is being built.
tasks.goal: Immediately deny known write/git/external-mutation tools and unknown-effect tools in plan mode; preserve explicitly classified read-only behavior, including only network reads allowed by the current product policy.
deliverable: Temporary conservative plan-mode gate covers git mutations, remote/custom/MCP/extension tools and subagent dispatch paths.
Known read-only tools remain available according to existing product policy; do not broadly ban read-only web search/fetch unless policy requires it.
R4 replaces the temporary table with reviewed effect metadata without opening a policy gap.
verification: Planned tests: TestPlanModeBlocksKnownMutatingBuiltins, TestPlanModeBlocksUnknownEffectTool, TestPlanModePreservesApprovedReadOnlyTools.
Exercise every registered git mutation and a fake MCP/custom side-effect through the real plan middleware; assert zero executor invocations.
tasks.commit_spec: Focused interim safety commit; annotate it as temporary and tie replacement to R4 effect metadata acceptance.

tasks.title: Specify Run ownership, terminal outcome and cleanup state
tasks.user_story: As a caller, I need to know separately whether execution stopped and whether its external effect is known.
tasks.goal: Define ExecutionState and Outcome as orthogonal state dimensions, per-run owner, terminal uniqueness, cancel and cleanup transitions, and RunSlot release conditions using current Assembly/Loop/TurnRunner/RunSlotGuard.
deliverable: State transition table for running, cancel_requested, draining, quiescent and quarantined versus success, error, cancelled and unknown.
Ownership and shutdown contract for readers, workers, child processes, event delivery, session commit and slot release.
Event envelope semantics for provisional output, sequence gaps and authoritative terminal projection.
verification: Design review walks concurrent tool cancellation, provider read timeout, non-cooperative Go tool, killable child process, EventStream full/timeout and shutdown races.
Must state that outcome unknown alone never releases a shared workspace mutation slot and no global unbounded join is allowed.
tasks.commit_spec: Reviewed contract artifact only; do not require a new runtime framework name or product code in the designer task.

tasks.title: Make provider and continuation terminal results truthful
tasks.user_story: As a user, stream read/parse failures, timeout, guard failure and continuation failure must never look like a complete successful answer.
tasks.goal: Propagate one typed terminal result through provider stream, loop and TurnRunner; close incomplete tool messages and apply OutputGuard before text is made visible.
deliverable: Stream contract distinguishes complete, failed, timed out and cancelled.
Output guard is part of streaming and generation; failure blocks or buffers output before disclosure.
Continuation errors remain errors and incomplete tool arguments are never dispatched.
verification: Planned tests: TestStreamReadErrorIsNotComplete, TestStreamMalformedEventIsNotComplete, TestStreamTimeoutIsNotComplete, TestOutputGuardRunsBeforeVisibleDelta, TestContinuationErrorReturnsFailure.
Use a local fixture server and actual CLI assembly; verify no successful final event and no tool execution after partial args.
tasks.commit_spec: Commit the terminal-contract implementation separately from retry policy; regression tests must be red on audited baseline.

tasks.title: Quiesce cancelled runs and close tool transcript pairs
tasks.user_story: As a user, cancellation must stop new work immediately while the UI truthfully reports any existing worker that is still cleaning up.
tasks.goal: Do not mark a Run terminal before workers finish, synthesize after caller cancellation, claim dropped subagent sends succeeded or discard tool history without a paired result/unknown receipt.
deliverable: Cancel request and terminal completion are distinct transitions.
Agent history closes each tool call by ToolCallID with result, interrupted or unknown semantics.
Subagent sends report accepted, rejected or backpressure, never false success.
Per-assembly interceptor/registry state does not leak between Assemblies.
verification: Planned tests: TestCancelDoesNotMarkRunQuiescentBeforeToolExit, TestUnknownOutcomeRetainsMutationSlot, TestCancelClosesToolCallHistory, TestSubagentSendReportsDroppedMessage, TestAssemblyInterceptorsAreIsolated.
Block a mutation worker on a channel; after bounded wait assert cleanup_pending/quarantined and second mutation is rejected; release/kill it and assert only then slot becomes available.
Exercise cancellation via real AssembleAgent and actual shared RunSlotGuard.
tasks.commit_spec: One commit for cancellation/history state machine and one for assembly scoping if independently reviewable; both must preserve current shared RunSlotGuard wiring.

tasks.title: Supervise workers and surface event/resource failures
tasks.user_story: As an operator, timeout, drop or shutdown must reveal what is still active and which result was not delivered.
tasks.goal: Make bounded EventStream errors observable to the owner, keep Harness span lifetime aligned with Run, and ensure output and worker cleanup cannot grow without bounds.
deliverable: Event drop/timeout returns a detectable gap or delivery error in Run state.
Harness root span covers asynchronous Run completion.
Worker shutdown is bounded and non-cooperative work is quarantined or isolated rather than falsely reported quiescent.
No unbounded output retention in remote Bash metadata.
verification: Planned tests: TestEventStreamDropVisibleToRunOwner, TestHarnessSpanEndsAfterRun, TestNonCooperativeWorkerQuarantinedAfterDeadline, TestRemoteBashMetadataRemainsBounded.
Inject a full 30-second-default projection using a test-configured short timeout; assert loss is surfaced and authoritative transcript remains complete.
tasks.commit_spec: Commit lifecycle/observability work in independently testable chunks; do not turn EventStream into the source of truth.

tasks.title: Prove terminal uniqueness and safe quiescence
tasks.user_story: As a release owner, I need cancellation and timeout behavior verified at the actual Run boundary.
tasks.goal: Independently verify one terminal result, no premature resource/slot release, and no false successful stream completion.
deliverable: Failure-injection report with each worker state and outcome pair.
Actual CLI subprocess evidence for child-process kill/join and non-cooperative worker bounded wait.
Race and leak evidence through production Run path, not only verify helper tests.
verification: Run all planned exact-name tests after asserting registration; run affected core/provider/tool packages with -race -count=1.
Kill CLI at provider-read, tool-start, tool-return and event-delivery seams; assert one terminal projection and no overlapping workspace mutation.
tasks.commit_spec: No builder code changes; create separate fix task for any rejected invariant and re-review that commit.

tasks.title: Define minimal durable transcript and recovery format
tasks.user_story: As a user, I need to resume a session after process exit and see which actions completed, failed or became unknown.
tasks.goal: Add the smallest incremental durable record contract that fits SessionTree and JSONL without full event sourcing, per-token fsync or automatic arbitrary action replay.
deliverable: Identity rules for physical session file, session ID, entry ID, branch/root parent and ToolCallID/ActionID.
Commit points for user input, tool intent, tool receipt/unknown, compaction projection, final response and flush/sync acknowledgment.
Recovery policy for complete lines, valid no-newline tail, truncated JSON tail, malformed complete record, duplicate IDs and unknown side effects.

On restart, idempotently complete a previously synced, locally validated execution-resolution checkpoint in the global workspace index; never replay the action and keep quarantine active until the global resolution sync succeeds.

Unresolved action records retain verifiable execution identity (not a bare PID); after parent CLI SIGKILL, recovery quarantines the conflicting session/workspace until child/process-group exit is proven or an operator reconciles it. Safe reads may continue.
verification: Review crash matrix before dispatch, after side effect before receipt, after receipt before final, during append/flush/sync.
Verify unknown action is surfaced for reconciliation and never auto-dispatched on reopen.

Inject a crash after session resolution checkpoint Sync but before global index append/Sync; recovery appends the exact resolution once, clears quarantine only after Sync, and performs zero tool/provider replay.

Kill the parent CLI while a child process continues writing; on restart, reject conflicting writes until independently verified exit or explicit quarantine reconciliation. Never kill based on a bare PID or clear a RunSlot as evidence.

During recovery, a workspace read is allowed only when the trusted resolved EffectSet proves read-only and the pinned executor enforces declared workspace/path scope; unknown effects and unscoped default Read/Grep/Find/Ls remain blocked during a conflicting quarantine.
tasks.commit_spec: Reviewed record-format and crash-policy note only; preserve existing JSONL compatibility or document a versioned migration before implementation.

tasks.title: Fix session identity, tree restoration and multi-process ownership
tasks.user_story: As a user, starting a new session cannot merge into another session, and resume must select the intended session and branch.
tasks.goal: Repair physical session identity/resume, append-only tree/branch projection, compaction restore provenance, lock-before-read/recovery, and defensive-copy/sequence behavior.
deliverable: Unique physical session file per session even within the same second.
Resume resolves file/session ID then entry/branch ID without ambiguous conversion.
Restored Agent history includes compaction summary and valid tool-call groups; branch Clone shares the immutable canonical prefix without copying or rewriting ActionID/ToolCallID authority.

Single-writer lock acquired before loading or repairing records; unsupported platforms fail closed; entry clones and sequence persistence are stable. Pending action recovery validates local resolution checkpoints and cannot expose a ready SessionView without the injected marker authority applying those checkpoints to the global index and inspecting the resulting markers.
JSONL record size policy is symmetric between append and reopen.
verification: Planned tests: TestNewSessionCreatesIndependentRootFile, TestResumeSessionIDSelectsTreeEntry, TestRestoreIncludesCompactionSummary, TestSessionLockAcquiredBeforeLoad, TestUnsupportedSessionLockFailsClosed, TestPendingActionsRequireRecoveryAuthority, TestRecoveryAuthorityMatchesEachPendingActionReference, TestRecoveryAppliesDurableExecutionResolutionAfterGlobalAppendCrashExactlyOnce, TestNeverDispatchedResolutionWithoutGlobalMarkerIsNoOp, TestResolutionConflictKeepsWorkspaceQuarantined, TestCloneSharesCanonicalPrefixWithoutRewritingToolCallIDs, TestCloneAppendsDivergeFromSharedLeaf, TestSessionTreeCloneDoesNotAliasNestedArgs, TestSessionSeqPersists, TestSessionSameSecondUsesUniqueFile, TestSessionLargeRecordRoundTrips.
Test record sizes at 1 MiB minus one, exactly 1 MiB and plus one; either read them back or reject before successful append.
Run actual CLI resume in a child process against a temporary session directory.
tasks.commit_spec: Separate identity/resume and loader/concurrency commits if contracts stay independent; each commit includes exact red-before-fix regression tests.
tasks.execution_scope: Accepted partial mappings include session RunCommitSink changes 63e9fd→1f2a19b, 75ceb→bf4bbcb, 5a6dd→82d47bc; CLI wrapper changes 29765ab→edc1f27 and docs 9a074→800fa65; and test-only callback fixture 1945e8→d3cfcf5. The adapter review accepted its bounded tests, but the integrated 5bf14e2 run exposed nine stale session fixture expectations later corrected by the test-only commit. Actual run-owner late-proof wiring, Loop/CLI/session restart integration, typed compaction provenance, and child/process recovery remain open; the real CommitCompaction consumer waits on R3. This task is not done.

tasks.title: Persist intent, receipt and truthful save acknowledgments
tasks.user_story: As a user, completed responses are recoverable, while a crash in an external action never causes silent duplicate execution.
tasks.goal: Propagate append/flush/sync errors, persist action intent/result at semantic commit points, recover unknown outcomes without replay and handle torn tails conservatively.
deliverable: Store writes create/append correctly for directory mode and fail to caller on append/flush/sync errors.

Typed Loop commit sink durably records input, complete assistant tool-call groups, per-action intent/reservation, receipts, resource-resolution checkpoints, compaction projection, and terminal commit at the defined semantic boundaries. RecoveryAuthority applies a session-validated resolution checkpoint to the global workspace index idempotently; the global index remains quarantined until its matching resolution append and Sync succeed.

Tool intent and workspace dispatch-ready marker are both durable before dispatch; R4 prepared invocation pins trusted identity/effects and exact executor. Result/unknown receipt and separate resource-resolution evidence are durable before the next provider request.
Final success/save UI acknowledgment follows durable commit.
Only demonstrably truncated final JSON is quarantined/truncated; valid JSON without newline is preserved and delimited; malformed complete lines fail closed.
Persist unresolved-action quarantine so a parent process crash cannot expose the same workspace to a conflicting mutation while its child/process group may still be running; do not kill by PID alone.
verification: Planned tests: TestAppendFailurePreventsSavedAck, TestToolIntentDurableBeforeDispatch, TestCrashAfterActionMarksUnknownWithoutReplay, TestUnknownReceiptWithLiveChildKeepsCrossSessionMutationBlocked, TestLateExecutionDoneResolvesQuarantineExactlyOnce, TestUnknownExecutorWithoutPendingExecutionErrorCannotResolveQuarantine, TestRecoveryAppliesDurableExecutionResolutionAfterGlobalAppendCrashExactlyOnce, TestNeverDispatchedResolutionWithoutGlobalMarkerIsNoOp, TestResolutionConflictKeepsWorkspaceQuarantined, TestValidJSONTailWithoutNewlineIsPreserved, TestTruncatedJSONTailIsQuarantined, TestMalformedCompleteJSONLineFailsClosed, TestDirectoryStoreAppendOpensWriter, TestPendingSavepointUsesAbsoluteEnqueueSequenceAcrossFlush, TestSessionSyncFailurePoisonsWriterUntilReopen, TestAssemblyToolSearchFilteringSurvivesProtectedListProxy.

Use injectable file writer failures and an actual child process killed after side effect but before receipt; assert side-effect count remains exactly one after restart. Kill the parent process while its child keeps writing; assert restart blocks conflicting writes but allows safe reads until verified child exit or explicit manual reconciliation.
No test should require fsync for each token; assert only declared semantic commit points.
Planned tests: TestRecoveryBlocksWorkspaceMutationWhileOrphanChildLives, TestRecoveryAllowsSafeReadWhileWorkspaceQuarantined.
tasks.commit_spec: One commit for durable journal and truthful acknowledgment; persistence format changes require explicit versioning and fixture compatibility tests.
tasks.execution_scope: Partial lane build_bash is preparing only the standalone durable workspace_index storage/RecoveryAuthority adapter and its tests. It may proceed without Loop/CLI wiring; do not connect it to dispatch until the R4 prepared-dispatch boundary is accepted. Cross-session marker matching, append+Sync/idempotency, quarantine and restart gates remain open, so this partial lane does not close R2-BLD-02 or R2.

tasks.user_story: As a release owner, I need evidence from a restarted real CLI, not only a mocked store or helper, that session recovery is complete and non-replaying.
tasks.goal: Review the recovered transcript and side-effect ledger across all declared crash points.

tasks.title: Fix retry, breaker, loop, budget accounting and safe output cleanup
tasks.user_story: As a user, transient failures and runtime limits must be handled predictably without retrying an action whose outcome may already have escaped.

tasks.title: Land trusted tool identity and effect metadata prerequisite
tasks.user_story: As a user, workspace quarantine must classify the actual registered executor, not trust a tool name or caller-supplied label.

deliverable: Immutable registry-bound executor identity and trusted EffectSet are queryable from the resolved executor/wrapper without relying on names or caller metadata.

A side-effect-free prepared-dispatch seam pins the exact executor, normalized call, registry/policy generations, and one-time authorization snapshot. After durable intent sync, direct execution checks the final shared fence before dispatch; a queued mutation consumes one-use admission at enqueue and rechecks that same fence at dequeue before captured execution, without name relookup.

MutationQueue preserves the captured execution stage and original context, rather than reconstructing a Write/Edit tool or bypassing the captured wrapper. A queue worker cannot re-enter public dispatch, approval, normalization or the queue. Registry List/wrappers cannot expose an unwrapped executable definition; protected proxies preserve Parameterized, StreamingBashTool, PromptGuideliner and TopToolsProvider capabilities.

Effect inventory covers derived execution; Git actions that may invoke repository-configured helpers remain unknown/composite until a trusted implementation disables those hooks or proves a restricted path.

The narrow seam is mapped to source R4-BLD-01. Full R4-BLD-01 retains its original source scope and remains pending until its complete approval/Plan Mode contract (including pending D-01) is implemented and reviewed.

Grep/fd receive no workspace_read effect until fixed-argument and child-environment hardening is present: ripgrep passes patterns with -e, terminates path options with --, uses --no-config and removes RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH; fd terminates options before user-controlled values and exposes no execution option. Helper-capable Git paths remain unknown/composite unless their captured executor disables or proves those helpers safe.
verification: Test same-name custom executor spoofing cannot inherit a built-in read-only identity/effect.
Test registry replacement/version changes produce distinct immutable executor identities.
Test approval Ask/allow and Ask/deny during preparation; no underlying executor starts before the durable dispatch boundary, and a stale registration/policy generation cannot dispatch.

Test a queued generation change is caught at dequeue; successful queued work executes the captured executor once and never re-enters approval/queue or re-resolves by tool name. Test ordinary and streaming dispatch share one permit and raw streaming proxies cannot bypass preparation.
Independent review verifies the trusted metadata is bound to the executor actually returned by the registry; no tool-name allowlist is accepted as proof.

Through the real prepared path, prove grep pattern --pre=sh plus injected RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH cannot run a helper, and fd pattern --exec plus an executable path cannot run a command; assert these registrations remain unknown until the hardening is implemented.
Verify git status/fsmonitor and diff/external-diff or textconv paths remain unknown/composite unless the captured executor disables the repository-configured helper or proves a restricted path.

tasks.title: Ship or clearly disable deferred product capabilities
tasks.user_story: As a user, a named command or tool must either work across restart and runtime wiring or explain that it is not available.
tasks.goal: Implement only capabilities selected in R8-DES-01; hide or mark dormant APIs that are not funded for this release.
deliverable: For selected ImageRead and persisted Goal/Task/Todo features, register in the default CLI and prove restart roundtrip.
For selected memory retrieval, connect it to runtime with bounded and explainable retrieval, or mark it manual-only.
For declined branch/snapshot/migration/Web/external extension paths, remove misleading help/status or return explicit unsupported.
If memory storage remains a supported path, append/delete errors leave in-memory indexes consistent with durable state; otherwise the affected persistence feature is clearly unavailable.
verification: Planned tests: TestImageReadAvailableInDefaultCLI, TestGoalTaskTodoSurviveRestart, TestMemoryRetrievalInjectedWhenEnabled, TestDormantCapabilityReportsUnsupported.
Run CLI subprocess restart journey for every capability actually selected; do not require tests for explicitly unavailable features beyond a clear unsupported result.
For Docker, validate the declared target architecture in build metadata or smoke each promised target; no ARM64 support is implied unless selected.
Planned tests: TestMemoryStoreAppendFailureDoesNotPublishMemory, TestMemoryStoreDeleteReopenFailureConsistent.
tasks.commit_spec: One commit per selected capability; documentation/hide-path changes may be separate. Feature implementation requires a named product acceptance, not audit inference.

tasks.title: Run final TUI, capability and evidence gate
tasks.user_story: As a release owner, I need the final supported feature list to match reproducible product behavior on supported platforms.
tasks.goal: Review real PTY behavior, startup/help claims, restart persistence and the complete evidence bundle before release.
deliverable: Final supported/partial/unclosed/unavailable matrix with source report mapping.
Cross-platform/terminal verification record and known limitations.
Current-commit gate logs; Phase status cannot substitute for them.
verification: Run exact named tests with registration assertion and package race suites.
Re-run local and CI-equivalent validation with command versions and env recorded; verify no stale generated/source changes from formatting checks.
tasks.commit_spec: Reviewer code-free; release matrix states separately source review, unit behavior, Runtime integration, protocol peer and PTY evidence.

tasks.title: Specify opt-in action replay eligibility and reconciliation
tasks.user_story: As a user who explicitly opts in, I want only verifiable idempotent actions to resume after a process crash.
tasks.goal: Define the smallest action class eligible for cross-process resume, with stable identity, receipt/verifier, generation fencing, cancellation and human reconciliation for unknown results.
deliverable: Per-tool replay eligibility and proof contract; shell and arbitrary MCP default to ineligible.
Explicit opt-in, status and manual reconciliation UX.
Threat and failure matrix for duplicate owner, stale generation, lost receipt and verifier failure.
verification: Do not proceed to build unless every supported action proves idempotency or durable receipt semantics and explicit product approval exists.
Unknown action remains unknown and cannot be interpreted as permission to retry.
tasks.commit_spec: No implementation commit unless product opts in and design passes a separate review.

tasks.title: Implement only receipt-verified opt-in resumable actions
tasks.user_story: As an opted-in user, a supported action may resume only when the stored receipt/verifier proves safe execution state.
tasks.goal: Add generation-fenced action claim, verification and explicit reconciliation without changing the R2 default unknown/no-replay behavior.
deliverable: Narrow allowlisted action executor with stable idempotency key and durable receipt.
Restart recovery that verifies before any resumed action and never reruns an action with ambiguous state.
UI status for verifying, resumable, resumed, failed verification and manual reconciliation.
verification: Planned tests: TestResumeActionRequiresExplicitOptIn, TestResumeActionVerifiesReceiptBeforeDispatch, TestResumeActionGenerationFence, TestUnknownActionRequiresReconciliation, TestDuplicateRecoveryOwnerCannotExecuteTwice.
SIGKILL duplicate-owner and receipt-corruption matrix; side-effect count remains one or execution is blocked.
tasks.commit_spec: No commit until R9 design is approved; retain default-disabled behavior behind explicit configuration and capability allowlist.

tasks.title: Audit replay safety independently before enabling
tasks.user_story: As a release owner, I need an independent proof that crash recovery cannot duplicate or wrongly suppress external actions.
tasks.goal: Review verifier soundness, receipt durability, fencing, opt-in scope and human reconciliation.
deliverable: Independent replay matrix and explicit eligible-action list.
Negative evidence for shell, MCP and every unverified action class remaining non-replayable.
Enablement recommendation per action, not blanket Runtime auto-resume approval.
verification: Run exact registered tests, package race suites and full CLI child-process SIGKILL tests with duplicated recovery owners.
Corrupt or remove receipt and verifier inputs; action must stop for reconciliation rather than dispatch.
tasks.commit_spec: Reviewer code-free; no action is enabled until a separate release decision accepts the written action-specific evidence.

evidence_policy.red: compiled test fails because baseline behavior violates the intended contract; compile failures and zero matches do not count
evidence_policy.green: same regression test passes and affected package race suite passes
